practiceQuestions.q: Who holds the ex-officio position of the Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) under the Indian Constitution?
opts: The Prime Minister of India
The Vice-President of India
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
A member elected by the Rajya Sabha from among themselves
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 64 and Article 89(1) of the Constitution of India explicitly state that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Article of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States?
opts: Article 85
Article 89
Article 93
Article 100
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 89 of the Constitution provides that the Vice-President of India shall be ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States and also requires the Council to choose a member to be Deputy Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q: How is the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States chosen?
opts: Nominated by the President of India
Appointed by the Prime Minister
Elected by the Rajya Sabha from amongst its members
Chosen by the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha alone
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 89(2), the Rajya Sabha must, as soon as possible, choose one of its members to be the Deputy Chairman whenever the office falls vacant.

practiceQuestions.q: To whom does the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States submit their resignation?
opts: The President of India
The Chairman of the Council of States
The Prime Minister
The Secretary-General of the Rajya Sabha
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 90(b), the Deputy Chairman resigns their office by writing under their hand addressed to the Chairman of the Council of States.

practiceQuestions.q: Is the Chairman of the Council of States a member of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: Yes, always
No, the Chairman is not a member of the House
Yes, but only as a nominated member
It is optional for the Vice-President to be a member
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (the Vice-President) is NOT a member of the House.

practiceQuestions.q: Under what circumstance does the Chairman of the Council of States exercise a casting vote?
opts: During any constitutional amendment bill
When there is an equality of votes in the House
At the beginning of every session
Whenever the Prime Minister advises him to do so
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 100(1) states that all questions at any sitting of either House shall be determined by a majority of votes of the members present and voting, other than the Speaker or person acting as such, and the Chairman or person acting as such shall not vote in the first instance, but shall have and exercise a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary procedural requirement for removing the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: A resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha
A simple majority of members present and voting in a joint sitting
An executive order issued by the President of India
Impeachment by both Houses of Parliament with a two-thirds majority
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 90(c) specifies that the Deputy Chairman may be removed from office by a resolution of the Council passed by a majority of all the then members of the Council, provided that a 14-day notice has been given.

practiceQuestions.q: Can the Chairman of the Council of States vote during the proceedings when a resolution for their own removal from office is under consideration?
opts: Yes, as an ex-officio member
No, because the Vice-President is not a member of the Rajya Sabha and cannot vote under any circumstances
Yes, with a special casting vote
Only if the Lok Sabha permits
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Chairman (Vice-President) is not a member of the Rajya Sabha, they never possess a primary vote in the House. Article 92 applies explicitly to the Chairman or Deputy Chairman presiding while a removal resolution is under consideration, but the Chairman inherently does not vote in the House under any routine capacity.

practiceQuestions.q: Under Article 91(1), who performs the duties of the office of the Chairman of the Council of States when the Vice-President acts as, or discharges the functions of, the President of India?
opts: The Prime Minister
The Deputy Chairman of the Council of States
The senior-most nominated member
The Chief Justice of India
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 91(1) states that during any period when the Vice-President is acting as President or discharging the functions of the President, the duties of the Chairman shall be performed by the Deputy Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum period of notice required to move a resolution for the removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: 7 days
14 days
21 days
30 days
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 90(c) explicitly requires a minimum notice of 14 days before a resolution for the removal of the Deputy Chairman can be moved in the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha not a member of the house he presides over, unlike the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: Because the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college comprising members of both Houses of Parliament, embodying a distinct federal executive-cum-legislative dual role.
Due to a clerical oversight in the drafting of the original Constitution by the Constituent Assembly.
To prevent the Chairman from ever participating in any legislative debates.
To give the Rajya Sabha absolute independence from the executive branch of government.
practiceQuestions.sol: The framers of the Constitution adopted the American model for the office of the Vice-President, who serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the upper house. Since the Vice-President is elected nationally by both houses to fill the second-highest executive office of the land, holding a regular constituency seat in the upper house is structurally unnecessary and anomalous.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the removal procedure of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha differ fundamentally from that of the Deputy Chairman?
opts: The Chairman is removed via impeachment initiated in the Lok Sabha.

The Chairman is removed from the office of Vice-President through a resolution of the Rajya Sabha agreed to by the Lok Sabha; there is no separate removal process solely for the Rajya Sabha chairmanship.
The Chairman can be removed by a simple majority vote of the Rajya Sabha alone.
The Chairman can only be removed by the Supreme Court of India.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the Vice-President of India. Therefore, to remove the Chairman from the chairmanship, the Vice-President must be removed from office. This requires a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha by a majority of all then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha. In contrast, the Deputy Chairman is removed by a resolution passed solely within the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q: When a resolution for the removal of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is under consideration in the House, what restriction is placed on the Chairman under Article 92?
opts: The Chairman cannot enter the Parliament building.
The Chairman cannot preside over the House during that sitting, though they may have the right to speak and take part in proceedings.
The Chairman must immediately resign from office.
The Chairman is stripped of all pensionary benefits permanently.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 92 explicitly stipulates that the Chairman or Deputy Chairman shall not preside while a resolution for their removal from office is under consideration. However, the Chairman (as Vice-President) has the right to speak and otherwise take part in the proceedings of the Council during such a time, though as a non-member they do not have a vote.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional implication regarding financial bills and money bills in relation to the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
opts: The Chairman certifies whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.
The Chairman has no power to certify a Money Bill; that authority rests exclusively with the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
The Chairman can introduce Money Bills in the Rajya Sabha.
The Chairman can veto any Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 110(4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha holds the exclusive power to certify a bill as a Money Bill. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has no role in certifying Money Bills, reflecting the structural dominance of the Lok Sabha in financial matters.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the administrative control over the Rajya Sabha Secretariat compare between the Chairman and the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
opts: The Chairman exercises independent administrative and disciplinary control over the Rajya Sabha Secretariat, mirroring the Speaker's control over the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
The Rajya Sabha Secretariat is directly controlled by the Union Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
The Chairman shares joint control with the President of India over all administrative appointments.
The Chairman has no administrative powers; all staff matters are handled by the Deputy Chairman.
practiceQuestions.sol: Just as the Speaker of the Lok Sabha heads and controls the Lok Sabha Secretariat independently, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha heads the Rajya Sabha Secretariat and holds supreme administrative and disciplinary authority over its officers and staff.

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of joint sittings of both Houses of Parliament under Article 108, who presides over such sittings?
opts: The Chairman of the Council of States
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Vice-President of India in his executive capacity
The Prime Minister of India
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 118(4) and Article 108 dictate that the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting of both Houses. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) never presides over a joint sitting because they are not a member of either house in the conventional sense and are constitutionally excluded from this role.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the significance of the Panel of Vice-Chairpersons in the Rajya Sabha?
opts: They permanently replace the Chairman whenever the Vice-President is busy with foreign affairs.
Nominated by the Chairman, any member from this panel can preside over the House in the absence of both the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman.
They are responsible for drafting constitutional amendment bills in the Rajya Sabha.
They form the electoral college for the election of the Deputy Chairman.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Rajya Sabha, the Chairman nominates a panel of vice-chairpersons from among the members. Any one of them can preside over the House in the absence of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman. A member of the panel does not have the right to preside when both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman seats are vacant (which requires a fresh election for Deputy Chairman).

practiceQuestions.q: How does the salary and allowances of the Chairman of the Council of States get determined and charged?
opts: Determined by Parliament by law and charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
Determined by executive ordinance of the President and paid out of the Contingency Fund of India.
Determined by the Rajya Sabha alone through a simple resolution.
Determined by the Reserve Bank of India governor.
practiceQuestions.sol: The salaries and allowances of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (as Vice-President) and the Deputy Chairman are determined by Parliament by law under Article 97 and are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India, meaning they are non-votable by Parliament.

practiceQuestions.q: What happens to the office of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha when the Rajya Sabha is dissolved?
opts: The Chairman must also resign along with all members.
The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is never dissolved; hence the question of dissolution does not arise.
The President assumes direct control of the Rajya Sabha chairmanship during dissolution.
A temporary Chairman is appointed by the Election Commission.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 83(1) explicitly states that the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) shall not be dissolved, being a permanent chamber where one-third of its members retire every second year. Consequently, the question of the Chairman's office being affected by house dissolution does not arise.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes the nature of the power exercised by the Chairman under the Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule)?
opts: Quasi-judicial power, decisions of which are subject to judicial review.
Purely executive discretion that cannot be challenged in any court.
Legislative rulemaking power requiring assent of the President.
Advisory power whose recommendations are non-binding on political parties.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha decides questions of disqualification on the ground of defection for members of the Rajya Sabha. The Supreme Court in Kihoto Hollohan case (1992) ruled that the presiding officer acts as a Tribunal in this capacity, exercising quasi-judicial powers which are subject to judicial review.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chairman of the Council of States:
1. The Chairman is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
2. The Chairman is removable from office by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Vice-President (Chairman) is elected by an electoral college consisting of BOTH elected AND nominated members of both Houses of Parliament (not just elected). Statement 2 is incorrect because removal of the Vice-President requires a resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha by a majority of ALL THEN members of the House and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, not a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States:
1. The Deputy Chairman is not subordinate to the Chairman; rather, they are directly responsible to the Rajya Sabha.
2. When the office of the Chairman is vacant, the Deputy Chairman automatically assumes all executive powers and functions of the President of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Deputy Chairman is elected by the Rajya Sabha from amongst its members and is directly responsible to the House, not subordinate to the Chairman. Statement 2 is incorrect: When the office of the Chairman (Vice-President) is vacant due to death, resignation, or removal, the Deputy Chairman performs the duties of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, but does NOT become the President of India (only the Vice-President acts as President when the presidential office is vacant, and when the Vice-President office itself is vacant, the Vice-President's executive role is not performed by the Deputy Chairman).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the casting vote of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman exercises the casting vote to maintain the status quo when votes are tied.
2. The Chairman is constitutionally bound to provide detailed reasons in writing whenever a casting vote is exercised.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Parliamentary convention dictates that a presiding officer exercising a casting vote generally votes to preserve the status quo (i.e., voting against a change, amendment, or bill unless explicit reasons warrant otherwise). Statement 2 is incorrect: There is no constitutional or statutory requirement for the Chairman to provide detailed written reasons for exercising a casting vote.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the removal process of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman:
1. A resolution for the removal of the Deputy Chairman can be moved only after giving a 14-day advance notice.
2. During the discussion on a resolution for the removal of the Chairman, the Chairman has the right to vote in the Rajya Sabha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Statement 1 is supported by Article 90(c) which mandates a 14-day notice for a Deputy Chairman removal resolution. Statement 2 is correct because the Chairman (Vice-President) is not a member of the Rajya Sabha and therefore never possesses a primary vote, even though Article 92 allows them to speak and participate in proceedings during their removal discussion.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing the powers of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. Both presiding officers have the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill.
2. Both presiding officers have the power to adjourn the House sine die or suspend sittings in times of grave disorder.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because only the Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to certify a Money Bill under Article 110(4); the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha has no such power. Statement 2 is correct: As the administrative and procedural heads of their respective houses, both the Speaker and the Chairman possess the authority to adjourn the House or suspend sittings during disorder.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the casual vacancies in the offices of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman:
1. If the office of the Chairman falls vacant, the Deputy Chairman performs the duties until a new Vice-President is elected.
2. If both the Chairman and Deputy Chairman offices are vacant simultaneously, the President appoints a member of the Lok Sabha to preside over the Rajya Sabha temporarily.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct under Article 91(1). Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 91(2) states that if both offices are vacant, such member of the Rajya Sabha as the President may appoint shall perform the duties (not a member of the Lok Sabha).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding parliamentary committees and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the ex-officio chairman of all parliamentary committees established by the House.
2. The Chairman appoints the chairpersons of all standing committees of the Rajya Sabha from among its members.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Chairman is ex-officio chairman of certain committees like the Business Advisory Committee and Rules Committee of the Rajya Sabha, but NOT *all* committees (e.g., Public Accounts Committee has members from both houses with its chairman appointed by the Lok Sabha Speaker). Statement 2 is correct: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha appoints the chairpersons of the Department-related Standing Committees and other parliamentary committees that fall under the jurisdiction of the Rajya Sabha.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional position of the Vice-President as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha:
1. The Constitution of India explicitly provides a separate salary for the Vice-President specifically for their role as Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
2. The Vice-President's emoluments as Chairman are drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: The Constitution does not assign a salary to the Vice-President *qua* Vice-President; rather, the Vice-President draws salary and allowances in their capacity as the ex-officio Chairman of the Council of States. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 97, salaries and allowances of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the voting rights of the presiding officers in the Indian Parliament:
1. Neither the Speaker of the Lok Sabha nor the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha can vote in the first instance during normal divisions in their respective houses.
2. Both the Speaker and the Chairman possess a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is a member of the House and *does* have a primary vote (though by convention they usually do not vote in the first instance, choosing to use only their casting vote; however, they *can* vote if they choose to, unlike the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha who is a non-member and never has a primary vote). Statement 2 is correct: Both have a casting vote under Article 100(1).

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional safeguards of the Rajya Sabha presiding officers:
1. The service conditions and salaries of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman cannot be varied to their disadvantage after their election/appointment.
2. The conduct of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman in relation to the discharge of their duties can be discussed freely in the Rajya Sabha without any restriction.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
opts: 1 only
2 only
Both 1 and 2
Neither 1 nor 2
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Under Article 97, the salaries and allowances payable to the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and their service conditions cannot be varied to their disadvantage after appointment. Statement 2 is incorrect because the conduct of the presiding officers in relation to the discharge of their duties cannot be discussed in the House except on a substantive motion for their removal; general debate or criticism of their rulings is barred by parliamentary rules and conventions.
